findings.title: RF-HOUSE birdsmouth notches 1.47in plumb out of an 11-7/8 TJI 230 bottom flange (flange is 1-1/2in)

evidence.measured: Seat plane z=242.25in (plate top); rafter underside is 13.28in plumb below the deck line (11.875*sqrt(1.25)); at the heel (x=4.0in, seat_run 3.5in) underside is z=243.72, so the notch is 1.47in deep and starts at x=1.06in. TJI 230 flange is 1-1/2in thick (1.68in plumb at 6:12): the seat removes essentially the whole bottom flange at the heel.
evidence.expected: Weyerhaeuser: do not cut or notch I-joist flanges; rafter ends take a plumb/bevel bearing cut with the bottom flange bearing full on the plate (beveled plate or beveled web stiffeners, TB-805 'TJI in rafter cut applications'). Note cites 'birdsmouth ... APA D710 10h'; 10h could not be read here, hence low confidence.
evidence.method: load model.pkl; rafter=roof.members[0]; top(x)=z1+0.5(x-0.5); bottom=top-11.875*sqrt(1.25); compare to SeatCut.plate_top_z_m=6.15315 m. Scratchpad F4/p9.py.

findings.source: https://www.techsupport.weyerhaeuser.com/hc/en-us/articles/201758510-TJI-joists-with-top-flange-notches (bottom flange notching: avoid); TB-805 not fetched
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the birdsmouth by a plumb-cut tail seated on a beveled bearing plate (D710 10q, already named as the alternative in ridge_beam_detail.md), or confirm TB-805 allows the 1.47in bottom-flange notch; update SeatCut/emitters, takeoff (plate), A-593 K1, and recheck H2.5A tie and eave blocking elevations.

findings.title: Canopy trusses bear only 2.75in on the 5.5in glulam headers: heel point is at the beam centreline

evidence.measured: BM-BW-RW spans x=69.25..74.75in (axis 72.0); BM-BW-RE 357.25..362.75 (axis 360.0). Truss bottom chords run x=72..360 (bearing axis to bearing axis), tails to 56/376. Bearing under each heel = 2.75in (half the beam); the outboard 2.75in of the glulam is under the tail. Garage walls by contrast: axis is the outer sheathing face, truss bears the full 5.5in plate (72.6..78.1).
evidence.expected: Truss bearing width on a header at least 3.5in (typical truss design minimum), ideally full 5.5in with the heel at the beam's outer face; fabricator drawing will state required bearing.
evidence.method: model.solids tag BM-BW-RW outline x; roofs[RF-BW-CANOPY].members truss p0/p1 (scratchpad p4.py, p6.py); build_truss_layout uses bearing.axis as bear_lo/bear_hi.

findings.source: TPI/ICC truss bearing practice; CLAUDE.md canopy notes (bearing run inset 3/4in along y only)
findings.proposed_fix: Either shift the heel/bear datum for beam bearings to the beam outer face (span becomes 290.75in, overhang from the face) or state bearing width on S-102.1 and ask the fabricator to confirm 2.75in; affects the canopy wind oracles (canopy-roof-plane-cascade) so treat as large.

findings.title: Truss heel lift treats the 3.5in top-chord depth as vertical: deck plane 3/16in low on garage and canopy (4:12)

evidence.measured: ridge_z = 143.000in = plate 88 + heel 3.5 + chord 3.5 + 48 (144in half-run at 4:12) exactly; eave_z 89.667.
evidence.expected: Top chord underside meets the heel 3.5in above plate; the chord is 3.5in measured perpendicular, 3.5*sqrt(1+(1/3)^2)=3.689in plumb, so deck underside at the heel should be 95.19in and ridge 143.19in (+0.19in).
evidence.method: roof.eave_z_m*39.3701 and ridge_z_m for RF-GARAGE (p4.py); needed = plate_top + heel + truss_chord_depth_m in truss_heel_lift_m.

findings.source: geometry; roof_geometry.py docstring says top-chord underside clears plate+heel
findings.proposed_fix: Multiply chord depth by the slope factor in truss_heel_lift_m (the house rafter path already uses 13.28in plumb). Moves garage/canopy plane 0.19in: re-bless goldens and the canopy wind oracles, so this is a budgeted cascade, not a quick fix.

findings.title: S-102.1/.2 truss schedule 'MAX LENGTH 24'-0"' is bearing-to-bearing; trusses are 26'-8" overall with 16in tails

evidence.measured: Schedule prints 24'-0" for T1/T2; TrussShape tail_lo/hi = 0.4064 m (16in) each end, footprint 56..376in = 320in = 26'-8".
evidence.expected: Fabricator orders overall length 26'-8" (or must be told the 16in tails are included).
evidence.method: Read S-102.1/S-102.2 member schedule; roofs[].footprint and truss p0/p1 + tails.

findings.proposed_fix: Print overall length (and note bearing span 24'-0") in the schedule.
